case_title: SRIPATI SINGH (SINCE DECEASED) THROUGH HIS SON GAURA V SINGH v. THE STATE OF JHARKHAND
high_court_outcome: Set aside order of trial court
neutral_facts: The appellant provided financial assistance of Rs. 2 crore to the respondent, who assured repayment by June/July 2015. Cheques were issued as part of the transaction. The cheques were dishonoured due to insufficient funds. The appellant filed a complaint under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act and Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code. The respondent filed a discharge application, which was rejected by the trial court. The High Court set aside the trial court's order, leading to this appeal. The Supreme Court examined whether the cheques issued as security for a loan could be considered as a criminal offence under Section 420 IPC or a civil matter under Section 138 NI Act. The Court held that the mere dishonourment of cheques does not establish criminal intent, and the case was primarily a civil dispute over a loan repayment.
